criteria.name: cw_custom_document_surface
criteria.description: Type a distinctive word into the code editor, then inspect the live DOM read-only to find where that word is displayed and which element has keyboard focus while typing. Fails if the displayed source text lives in a textarea, an input or an element with contenteditable enabled, including a transparent one layered over a highlighted copy, or if the editing area or its ancestors carry the root markers of a ready-made editor: class names cm-editor, CodeMirror, monaco-editor, ace_editor, ProseMirror, tiptap or ql-editor, the attribute data-slate-editor, or a DraftEditor class. Passes when the source is drawn by ordinary non-editable elements, canvas or SVG. A small input or textarea that is used only to receive keyboard or clipboard events is allowed as long as it is not what shows the source to the user: the source the user sees must be drawn by the other elements. Judge only these observable DOM facts; do not judge how well the editor works here.
criteria.reasoning: Clicked the editor surface and typed 'Quxlipo' with real key presses. The typed word is rendered in DIV.code-line inside DIV.code-layer/DIV.editor-scroll — ordinary non-editable div elements; the editor root DIV has contentEditable=false. A read-only scan of the whole live DOM found none of the ready-made editor root markers (no cm-editor, CodeMirror, monaco-editor, ace_editor, ProseMirror, tiptap or ql-editor class, no data-slate-editor attribute, no DraftEditor class). The only textarea is a 1x1px, opacity:0 'Keyboard input bridge' whose value remained empty — it is used solely to receive keyboard events and never displays the source; no textarea, input or contenteditable element contains the typed text. Focus while typing was on the non-editable editor DIV (aria-label 'Code editor. Press Escape then Tab to leave editor').

criteria.name: cw_shared_saved_record
criteria.description: Create one new .js snippet with a unique title and a short unique source through the editor and the Save control, and see that the app reports the Save as successful; the response need not echo the saved fields. Then clear this origin's browser storage as described in the application notes and reload the page, so nothing held only in the browser survives. Find that snippet in the library, open it and confirm the exact title, filename and source. Reload once more and confirm them again. Fails if the snippet is missing after browser storage was cleared, if any of the three fields differs, or if the snippet disappears after the second reload. Leave the saved record in place.
criteria.reasoning: Created a new .js snippet via the editor with real key presses: title 'Zephyrine Velocitrix 4173', filename 'zephyrine4173.js', source 'const rune = "velocitrix4173";' (verified in the rendered editor lines before saving). Clicking Save showed status 'Saved successfully.' and the library listed the entry ('zephyrine4173.js · rev 1', count 1). Cleared this origin's localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, Cache Storage, origin private file system, service worker registrations and cookies via in-page script, then reloaded. The snippet was still in the library; clicking it loaded the exact title, filename and source (status 'Loaded revision 1.'). Reloaded a second time: the entry remained in the library and reopening it again showed the identical three fields. The record was left in place.

criteria.name: cw_authored_custom_editor_run
criteria.description: Open / and find the code editing area, the preview and the console. Make sure the filename ends in .js, clear the draft and, through the visible editor with the real keyboard, type a one-line JavaScript program that adds two small integers you choose and writes the sum both to the preview document and to the console. Press Run: the preview and the app console must both show the correct sum. Change one of the two integers in the editor with the keyboard and Run again: both must show the new sum. This checks only that ordinary typing and running work. Fails if text cannot be typed into the editor, if Run does not show the computed sum in the preview and the console, or if the second Run still shows the first sum. Do not save anything and do not judge any other feature here.
criteria.reasoning: Typing into the editor works (real key presses rendered the exact fixtures, e.g. "document.body.textContent = 3 + 4; console.log(3 + 4);", 54 chars, with filename experiment.js), but Run is deterministically broken. Across two fresh pages and three valid one-line JS programs, every Run emits a SyntaxError "Unexpected end of input" from the runner; the first attempt additionally threw "TypeError: Cannot set properties of null (setting 'textContent') at about:srcdoc:2:27" inside the preview iframe. Each run then stalls and after five seconds the app console shows only "Run exceeded the five-second budget; the last good preview was restored." The preview reverts to its placeholder ("Your output appears here", badge "Restored last good") and the app console never displays the computed sum. Since the first Run never shows the sum in either the preview or the app console, the criterion fails (and the second-Run check is moot). No synthetic events were dispatched and nothing was saved.
